chung.Description: This course provides an overview of how information systems support business operations, decision-making, and digital transformation in modern organizations. Students will explore core topics such as business processes, enterprise systems, databases, networks, cybersecurity, e-commerce, knowledge management and artificial intelligence. The course emphasizes how organizations use information systems strategically to achieve operational excellence, improve decision-making, and gain competitive advantage, so that learners know how information systems are transforming global business, and why they are so essential for running and managing a business today. Through real-world case studies and practical activities, students will analyze the structure of digital firms, model business processes, and evaluate system solutions. Key technologies such as cloud computing, data analytics, and business intelligence are introduced. Ethical and social issues related to data and systems use are also discussed. The course bridges business needs with IT capabilities, equipping students with foundational knowledge to work at the intersection of business and technology.

taiLieu: Management Information Systems: Managing the Digital Firm
clo: Explain the foundational concepts of information systems, including their definition, core components (management – organization – technology), the role of IS in digital enterprises, and the relationship between IS and business processes

Analyze the components of modern IT infrastructure, including cloud computing, mobile platforms, data storage and database management systems, computer networks, and emerging technologies such as IoT, AI, and data analytics
Apply knowledge of enterprise systems (ERP, SCM, CRM) and e-commerce systems to analyze how organizations achieve operational excellence and competitive advantage in a digital environment

Evaluate information strategies and digital business models using analytical frameworks such as Porter's Five Forces, the Value Chain Model, and global IS architecture, in order to propose IS solutions aligned with organizational objectives

Model and analyze business processes, identify business process redesign (BPR) opportunities enabled by IS, and select appropriate system development methodologies (SDLC, Agile, RAD, Prototyping) for given organizational contexts

Work with relational databases, Business Intelligence tools, and fundamental data analytics techniques (OLAP, data mining, dashboards) to support decision-making across different management levels within an organization

Identify and analyze information security risks, ethical, social, and legal issues in IS use (privacy, intellectual property, legal liability), and propose appropriate security controls and governance policies

Articulate the principles of IS project management, assess system implementation risks, and analyze the unique challenges of building and operating information systems in the context of global business organizations
